# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).
data.title: Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

# Intake Draft — Double-click heading to expand/collapse

**Work item:** WL-0MT2S3LMW0016DN3

## Problem statement

The Herdr selection list supports Tab-to-toggle group collapse on heading rows (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94 T3), but there is no mouse shortcut for this operation — a double-click on a heading row currently does nothing useful (it falls through to `open-detail` which is a no-op for headings since `getSelectedItem()` returns null). Power users who navigate with the mouse would benefit from a double-click-to-collapse pattern that mirrors the keyboard Tab behaviour.

## Users

- **Herdr plugin users** (operators running the work-item selection list pane) who use mouse interaction (click, double-click, wheel) alongside keyboard navigation.

User stories:
- "As a producer reviewing the worklist with a mouse, I want to double-click a group heading to collapse/expand it, so I can quickly hide groups I'm not interested in."
- "As a producer, I want double-clicking a heading to work the same way as pressing Tab on a heading, so my muscle memory carries across keyboard and mouse."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** Double-clicking a group heading row (two left presses on the same row within `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS`) toggles that group's collapse state — collapsed hides the group's items from render and navigation; expanded shows them.
- **AC2:** Double-clicking a work item row continues to open the detail view (existing behaviour unchanged).
- **AC3:** Single-clicking a heading row selects it (existing behaviour unchanged).
- **AC4:** The group collapse toggle on double-click preserves the existing in-memory state model (`collapsedGroups` Set, survives refresh, no persistence across restarts).
- **AC5:** When a heading is collapsed via double-click, the selection clamps to a visible item (the heading stays visible, but the collapsed items disappear).
- **AC6:** Full herdr test suite passes with the new changes.
- **AC7:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments.

## Constraints

- The change is confined to the Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr`) — specifically `worklist.ts` and its test files.
- Must be consistent with the existing mouse interaction model (double-click window, click tracking, drag-vs-click isolation).
- The Tab-key toggle for headings (WL-0MT1JGTJR002RTCB) must not regress.
- The renderer must never exceed `rows - 1` lines.

## Existing state

- Display-rows model (`WorkItemListState.getDisplayRows()`) interleaves `DisplayHeadingRow` objects with `WorkItem` objects.
- `isHeadingRow(row)` type guard identifies heading rows.
- `WorkItemListState.toggleGroupCollapse(group)` toggles a group's entry in the `collapsedGroups` Set.
- `handleKeypress` with `toggle-expand` on a heading row calls `toggleGroupCollapse` + `clampSelection` (lines ~3404–3414).
- `mapMouseToAction` double-click handling in list mode maps to `open-detail` for any non-null row index (line ~3738).
- `handleMouseInput` dispatches `open-detail` which calls `getSelectedItem()` — returns `null` for headings, so no-op (line ~3971).
- `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS = 400` (line 3453).
- `MouseClickState` tracks `lastClick { x, y, at }` for double-click detection.

## Desired change

1. **Add `toggle-group-collapse` action** to the `MouseAction` union type in `worklist.ts`.
2. **In `mapMouseToAction`** — when a double-click is detected in list mode, resolve the display row at the clicked index. If it is a heading row (`isHeadingRow`), return `{ type: 'toggle-group-collapse' }` instead of `{ type: 'open-detail' }`.
3. **In `handleMouseInput` dispatch** — add a case for `toggle-group-collapse` that calls `state.toggleGroupCollapse(row.group)` and `state.clampSelection()`, mirroring the keyboard `toggle-expand` heading path.
4. **Tests** — update `worklist-mouse.test.ts` to cover double-click on heading rows toggling collapse, and verify single-click, double-click on items, and double-click on different rows still work correctly.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `MouseAction` type, `mapMouseToAction` double-click logic, `handleMouseInput` dispatch case
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` — test coverage for heading double-click toggle

## Assumptions

- Double-click on heading = toggle group collapse (same as Tab on heading). This is the natural mapping and matches user expectations from other list-based UIs (file explorers, etc.).
- The heading row stays visible after collapse (items disappear, heading remains as the group label) — consistent with existing Tab-toggle behaviour.
- No visual feedback beyond the existing collapse indicator (arrow) changing — no additional animation or flash required.
- The `DOUBLE_CLICK_WINDOW_MS` constant (400 ms) is reused — no new timing threshold needed.

## Risks & Mitigations

- **Risk:** Double-click on heading could conflict with drag-to-scroll if a user accidentally double-presses. Mitigation: the double-click detection is strict (same coordinates, within window) — a drag that crosses the threshold restores the pre-press selection (AC3 of drag isolation). A genuine double-press (no motion past threshold) is a valid toggle.
- **Risk:** The `mapMouseToAction` change must correctly identify heading rows from a screen-row coordinate. Mitigation: use the existing `mapListRowToIndex` + `getDisplayRows()[index]` + `isHeadingRow` — this is the same pattern the keyboard path uses to distinguish heading from item selection.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Adding click-to-toggle (single click) would change the interaction model and could interfere with selection — this is out of scope. Only double-click is requested.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94** — Herdr selection list: collapsible group headings with item counts (parent feature — display-rows model, heading selection, Tab toggle).
- **WL-0MT1JGTJR002RTCB** — T3: Tab toggle for group collapse (keyboard toggle path for heading rows).
- **WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ** — Herdr selection list: mouse and touch support (mouse interaction model, double-click for detail view, drag-to-scroll).
- **WL-0MSI72S0Y0060BRK** — Drag-to-scroll implementation (drag-vs-click isolation).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should double-click on a heading toggle collapse (like Tab) or open something? — Answer (assumption, consistent with keyboard): toggle group collapse, same as Tab on heading. Source: the request says "double clicking a heading should expand/collapse it."
- Q: Should single-click on a heading toggle? — Answer (assumption, no): single-click selects the heading (existing behaviour); only double-click toggles. Single-click toggle would conflict with the selection model. Source: operator did not request single-click toggle; keyboard path uses Enter as no-op, Tab as toggle.
- Q: Does the heading stay visible when collapsed? — Answer (assumption, yes): heading stays visible as a group label; only the items in that group are hidden. Source: consistent with existing Tab-toggle behaviour (WL-0MT1JGTJR002RTCB).
data.title: double clicking a heading should expand/collapse it

Discovered-from: WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH.

When the audit runner runs child audits in separate-process mode (`--no-child-in-main-slot`), each child Phase-1 AC screen spawned a pi subprocess whose output could not be parsed: 'Warning: Unparseable Pi output for AC evaluation — falling back to partial verdict'. All child ACs were persisted as partial ('Ready to close: No'), which then reverted the in_review children to open/plan_complete and (via dependency reconciliation) to blocked — cascading a parent audit to 'Ready to close: No' even though the parent's own ACs were all met.

The default in-main-slot mode avoids this (child screens are performed by the invoking session), which is how the parent was ultimately verified green. Suggest: make separate-process child screening resilient to the local-proxy output format (or detect the unparseable case and retry/escalate instead of persisting partial), so the mode is usable in this environment.
data.title: Audit runner: separate-process child audits return unparseable pi output (falls back to partial)

Same latent hermeticity defect as WL-0MU2FM1L60002URI, found while fixing it: several worklist test files match herdr CLI calls with `bin === 'herdr'`. Because `isPaneVisible()` / pane helpers resolve the CLI as `process.env.HERDR_BIN_PATH ?? 'herdr'`, those mocks silently miss whenever the suite runs inside a herdr pane (which sets HERDR_BIN_PATH to an absolute path), and the call falls through to the mock's generic branch — which can flip a visibility probe to fail-open 'visible'.

Verified call sites (argument-based matching is the fix): packages/herdr/src/worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts:114, worklist-agent-state.test.ts:78, worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts:121,200, worklist-icons.test.ts:89, worklist-inflight.test.ts:102, worklist-nested-expand.test.ts:128, fetcher-timeout.test.ts:113,374.

Currently non-blocking: the full suite is green (the affected assertions do not depend on the missed branch), so this is hardening, not a live failure. Discovered from: WL-0MU2FM1L60002URI.
data.title: Harden remaining exec mocks against HERDR_BIN_PATH (match herdr calls by args, not binary name)

## Summary

`test/tmp_mig/worklog.db` is committed to git but is deleted and recreated by `test/migrations.test.ts` on every test run. This makes the file show as modified after any full-suite run, so `implement.py finish`'s `git add -A` commits a spurious binary change unless the file is explicitly protected with `git update-index --skip-worktree`.

## Expected behaviour

The test should write its scratch database to a temp directory outside the tracked tree (e.g. `os.tmpdir()`), or the artifact should be removed from git and added to `.gitignore`.

## Evidence

- `test/migrations.test.ts:7` — `const tmpDir = path.join(__dirname, 'tmp_mig')`
- Observed modified after `npx vitest run` during WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K.

## Summary

`test/tmp_mig/worklog.db` is a **test artifact** created and deleted by `test/migrations.test.ts` (its `beforeEach` unlinks the DB and clears the dir), but it is tracked in git and not gitignored. Every full-suite run rewrites it, so `implement.py finish` (which commits all worktree changes) includes a meaningless binary diff in the implementation commit.

Observed while implementing **WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV**: commit `ab2fb518` includes `test/tmp_mig/worklog.db | Bin 36864 -> 36864 bytes`; previous commits `cfdb9651` and `f19c74b6` carry the same churn.

## Desired behaviour

- `test/tmp_mig/` (or at least the generated `worklog.db`) is not tracked; add it to `.gitignore` and `git rm --cached` the existing file.
- Optionally have `test/migrations.test.ts` use an OS temp dir (like `tests/` does with `createTempDir()`) so it never writes inside the repo.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `test/tmp_mig/worklog.db` is no longer tracked and `test/tmp_mig/` is gitignored.
2. Running the full suite leaves `git status` clean (no binary churn).
3. `test/migrations.test.ts` still passes.
4. Full project test suite passes.

# Record the fast/cheap proxy slot-count contract

## Why

The drain-before-cheap feature failed because it hardcoded a cheap-pool budget (2) that no longer matched the proxy config. The cheap pool was silently changed from 2 to 3 slots, and fast is 1 slot -- the inverse of the brief's assumption.

## Scope

- Record the current mode slot counts and where they live:
  - fast = 1 slot (`llm-manager/proxy/config.yaml`: `session_slot_pool_size: 1`; `config-fast.yaml` does not override)
  - cheap = 3 slots (`llm-manager/proxy/config-cheap.yaml`: `session_slot_pool_size: 3`)
- State the contract: client/proxy-consumer logic MUST NOT hardcode pool sizes; derive from live status or not at all.
- Note the change history (cheap 2 -> 3) and the risk of silent drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The slot-count contract and both source locations are documented (README or docs/design).
- [ ] A pointer exists from the mode-switch design doc to the contract.
- [ ] No production code change (documentation only).
data.title: Document the fast/cheap proxy slot-count contract for client logic

Discovered from WL-0MURJ0LFH002O95I.

The r i (producer interview) fix added tab focus to run-in-pane.sh: a focused pane anchored to a work-item-ID tab now runs herdr tab focus before the pane zoom, because pane zoom alone cannot switch tabs.

shared/send-to-pi.sh has the same latent gap: its --focus path only runs pane zoom. No bundled agent shortcut currently combines focus: true with a work-item ID (P n has no <id>, so it opens in the current tab — a no-op today), so this is not user-visible yet. If a future --focus agent shortcut carries an <id>, its pane would open in the work-item-ID tab without focusing it.

Apply the same best-effort tab-focus (herdr pane get <pane> -> herdr tab focus) to send-to-pi.sh, mirroring run-in-pane.sh, with bash tests in packages/herdr/shared/tests/.

Discovered from: WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN (producer-rejection fix).

The default-view refresh path opens a FRESH WorklogDatabase connection per withInProcessDb call — twice per refresh (fetchActionableCount + fetchChildrenForItems). Each open is a synchronous better-sqlite3 operation (~46-70 ms on the 100 MB worklog.db, including initializeSchema/initializeFts DDL) that blocks the TUI event loop. After the WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN loop fix (counter-only watch), refreshes are occasional so this is a transient hiccup, not continuous lag; but it violates the strict reading of the <=100 ms p95 input-lag budget when a refresh coincides with typing.

Proposal: open ONE connection per refresh, share it between the actionable-count and children reads, close in a finally; or move the in-process read off the critical render path. Keep the no-stale-cache invariant (never serve from the store's in-memory query cache across a refresh boundary) by still closing per refresh.
data.title: Herdr: share one in-process SQLite connection per refresh to bound event-loop blocking

# Feature: Exclude dev + remote-tracking refs from guard diff

**Parent:** WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U (Finish-gate live-repo guard trips on concurrent dev ref movement in multi-agent repos)
**Issue type:** feature (implementation slice)

## Summary

Helper-only change in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`: `diff_snapshots` and `fingerprint` ignore the `refs/heads/dev` ref and the whole `refs/remotes/origin/*` namespace, so concurrent movement of these refs by sibling agents (finish fast-forwards on the shared main checkout, concurrent fetch/push) can no longer fail the live-repo mutation guard. Because both consumers (F4 outer `run_tests.py:guarded_run_all`, F5 inner `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`) share the helper, neither needs a code change and they cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `diff_snapshots` and `fingerprint` both report no change when only `refs/heads/dev` and/or `refs/remotes/origin/*` refs moved (movement or churn inside those namespaces is invisible).
- [ ] AC2 — Every other ref addition/removal/movement (e.g. fixture-branch creation like the incident's `feature-x` / `wl-*-test`), every local-config rewrite outside excluded branches, and every working-tree change still reports `changed == true` and fails the guard.
- [ ] AC3 — Existing exclusions are behaviour-preserving: `refs/worklog/*`, agent-worktree branch refs plus their `branch.<name>.*` config, and main-checkout anchoring all behave as before (existing regression tests stay green).
- [ ] AC4 — Helper-only: no consumer code change in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` or `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`; the F1 guard-level regression tests (inner + outer) pass via the shared helper.
- [ ] AC5 — Exclusion is expressed as ref-namespace constants (`refs/remotes/origin/` prefix, `refs/heads/dev` exact) — never a `wl-*` name pattern; snapshots stay read-only plumbing; the per-test `fingerprint` stays cheap (no `status` scan).
- [ ] AC6 — The full project test suite (pytest + node, as declared by the test skill) passes with the change.

## Target outcome
